title: CBS Cancels Stephen Colbert’s ‘Late Show,’ Citing Costs
content:
The Late Show with Stephen Colbert will air its last episode in May of next year, marking the end of the franchise, Paramount Global’s CBS network said.
Colbert, who has hosted the program for a decade, announced the show’s end during a taping on Thursday. He said he learned about the network’s decision the day before. Colbert replaced comedian David Letterman, who created and hosted the program for 22 years. “This is purely a financial decision against a challenging backdrop in late night,” CBS executives said in a joint statement. “It is not related in any way to the show’s performance, content or other matters happening at Paramount.”
Audience members at the Thursday taping booed at the news of the show’s demise.
“I’m not getting replaced,” Colbert said in an Instagram clip of his announcement, where he thanked all his supporters. “This is all just going away.”  Bloomberg News Media and Entertainment Editor Felix Gillette reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

content: European leaders will visit their Japanese and Chinese counterparts this week, and the expected outcomes reflect forces ranging from war to tariffs that are redrawing global trade relationships.

title: A ‘MAGA Monetary Policy Cocktail’ Comes Into View for the Fed
content: I’m Chris Anstey, an economics editor in Boston. Today we’re looking at an argument for Fed policy tools helping Main Street versus Wall Street. Send us feedback and tips to ecodaily@bloomberg.net. And if you aren’t yet signed up to receive this newsletter, you can do so  here.

title: Bank of England Considers Shelving Plans for a Digital Pound
content: Bank of England officials are mulling whether to set aside plans to create a digital pound for households amid growing skepticism about the project’s benefits, the latest sign of dwindling support for state-backed digital currencies globally.

title: UK Shoppers Face Extra £275 Grocery Bill on Higher Prices
content: UK food inflation nudged higher in the four weeks to mid-July as shoppers start to feel the burden of bigger grocery bills at the checkout.

title: China Launches Inspections to Halt Excessive Coal Production
content: The Chinese government warned it may shutter coal mines guilty of producing above permitted levels, in the latest sign that regulators are getting serious about reining in overcapacity across industries.

title: Morgan Stanley Faces Finra Probe on Client-Vetting, WSJ Says
content: Morgan Stanley is being probed by the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority over its vetting of clients for risk of money laundering, the Wall Street Journal reported.

title: Oakland Coliseum Is Sold as Developer Plans $5 Billion Overhaul
content: An Oakland-based developer has assumed full ownership of the Oakland-Alameda County Coliseum, paving the way for the revitalization of the deteriorating California complex.

title: NAB CEO Irvine Says Scrutiny on Behavior Made for Difficult Week
content: National Australia Bank Ltd. Chief Executive Officer Andrew Irvine said he’d faced a difficult week for himself and his family after a report surfaced about the leader’s managing style and drinking at client events.

title: America Movil’s Income Misses as Prepaid Disconnections Rise
content: Billionaire Carlos Slim’s wireless provider America Movil SAB’s net income missed analyst estimates as prepaid subscriber disconnections reached more than a million in the quarter.

title: Televisa Beats Estimates as Cable Subscriber Disconnects Slow
content: Grupo Televisa SAB reported higher profits than analysts expected, as the company’s improvements to its cable operations helped reduce churn.

title: US Defense Fuels Expanding $613 Billion Global Space Economy
content: The Pentagon’s spending on space grew faster than space-related military outlays by other nations in 2024, with the American total likely to soar as President Donald Trump’s administration moves ahead with his proposed Golden Dome missile shield.

title: Lockheed Flags $1.6 Billion in Charges as New CFO Digs Deep
content: Lockheed Martin Corp. caught investors off guard with $1.6 billion in charges and a possible tax hit that sent its stock tumbling, the latest setback for the defense giant whose popular F-35 jet faces criticism over cost overruns and delays.

title: Roche Pauses Shipments of Contested Gene Therapy Outside the US
content: Roche Holding AG paused all shipments of the controversial gene therapy Elevidys following a similar action by the embattled US biotechnology company that developed the treatment.

title: Tesla’s California EV Sales Drop for Seventh Straight Quarter
content: The number of new Tesla Inc. vehicles registered in California fell once again as the company continued to lose ground in the largest US market for electric vehicles.

title: Justin Bieber, Shakira Royalties to Back Bonds Sold by Recognition
content: Recognition Music Group, which manages a broad catalog of popular music, is selling $372 million of bonds backed by royalties from the likes of Red Hot Chili Peppers, Journey, Justin Bieber, and Shakira.

title: Fenway Park Concession Workers Plan Strike After Wage Talks Fail
content: About 1,000 workers who staff concession stands at Fenway Park baseball stadium — the iconic home of the Boston Red Sox — and the MGM Music Hall next door are poised to go on strike after negotiations between their union and food service company Aramark failed.

title: UniCredit Drops BPM Takeover Bid Amid Government Opposition
content: UniCredit SpA dropped its bid for rival Banco BPM SpA, ending an eight-month standoff with its rival and the Italian government over the plan to create the country’s largest lender.

title: LA Filming Declines 6.2% With Hollywood Movies Shooting Abroad
content: Movie and TV filming in the Los Angeles area declined 6.2% in the second quarter, an improvement from a 22% slump earlier in the year, but still indicative of the challenges California faces in competing for the business with other states and countries.

title: Synovus Weighs Potential Merger After Drawing Takeover Interest
content: Synovus Financial Corp., a regional bank in the southeastern US, is weighing options including a potential merger after drawing interest, people familiar with the matter said.

title: Dassault Reiterates Goal to Lead Franco-German Warplane Project
content: France’s Dassault Aviation SA reiterated it wants to lead the Franco-German next-generation Future Combat Air System fighter jet, giving it sweeping oversight over the project that’s caused friction with partner Airbus SE.

title: Hershey Raising Candy Prices by Double Digits on High Cocoa Costs
content: Hershey Co. is raising prices on its candy due to historically high cocoa costs.

title: Dassault Aviation’s Private Jet Orders Drop as Tariffs Loom
content: Orders for Dassault Aviation SA’s Falcon business jets dropped to their lowest level in five years as the threat of tariffs delay assembly and keep customers at bay.

title: Billionaire Fired From Polish Media Firm He Founded in Family Feud
content: In Poland, one of the country’s biggest media businesses is embroiled in a rapidly escalating family dispute that’s playing out like a real-life version of the hit television show ‘Succession.’

title: MasOrange’s PE Owners Seek At Least €5 Billion for 50% Stake
content: The private equity owners of MasOrange are seeking at least €5 billion ($5.9 billion) for their combined 50% stake in the Spanish telecommunication joint venture, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: HPS, Arcmont Provide €25 Million in Fresh Funds to Dainese
content: HPS Investment Partners and Arcmont Asset Management provided €25 million ($29.3 million) of fresh funding to ailing Italian sportswear maker Dainese SpA as part of broader negotiations that could see the private-credit funds take over the business.

title: Kellanova to Remove Synthetic Dyes From Retail Foods by 2028
content: Kellanova said it’s on track to remove synthetic food dyes from its retail foods by 2028, following similar moves from other packaged-food companies as President Donald Trump’s administration pressures the industry to remove the additives.

title: Billionaire Thomson Family to Buy £25 Million Luxury London Apartment
content: A member of the multibillionaire family behind Thomson Reuters Corp. agreed to buy a high-end London apartment for about £25 million ($34 million), in the latest sign of North Americans bolstering the city’s luxury market.
